title: What to Pack for Universal: The Locker Problem
h1: What to Pack for a Universal Trip
metaDescription: Universal makes you put everything in a locker before half its coasters, which changes what you carry. A park bag list for Orlando humidity and a hillside.
summary: A park bag list built around the thing that makes Universal different: mandatory free lockers before many of the big rides, enforced hard, with banks that back up worse than the ride does. Pack for that and the rest follows.
intro: Universal has a packing constraint no Disney park imposes, and it should shape your bag more than the weather does. At many of the big rides you cannot take anything with you. Not a small bag, not a phone in a zipped pocket, not a hat. Everything goes into a locker bank before you board, and the loose-article policy is enforced with metal detectors at the platform.

The lockers are free for a posted duration that covers the ride, and they charge beyond it. The problem is not the cost — it is the throughput. The locker bank at a busy coaster routinely backs up worse than the ride itself does, and a party of four fumbling with a touchscreen while holding four bags is how twenty minutes disappears twice a day.

The correct response is to carry dramatically less than you would at a Disney park. A large backpack is an active liability at Universal Orlando in a way it simply is not at Magic Kingdom. Almost everything else on this page follows from that one fact.

The second constraint is water. Three rides at Islands of Adventure will make you wet and two of them will soak you through to the skin, and Universal does not mist people the way Disney does. Plan for genuinely wet clothes rather than a damp shoulder, and the afternoon becomes the best part of a Florida day instead of the worst.
keyPoints: Many Universal coasters require every loose article in a locker before boarding, enforced with metal detectors at the platform.
Lockers are free for a posted duration and the banks back up worse than the rides do. Carry less and you skip the problem entirely.
Wear shorts with fewer pockets. Every pocket is something a team member has to check and something you have to empty.
If your party is using Child Swap, the waiting adult holds all the bags and nobody in the group touches a locker.
Three rides at Islands of Adventure soak you properly. Bring spare socks and a dry shirt, and put them in the locker rather than the bag.
Ponchos handle Dudley Do-Right's Ripsaw Falls and do very little on Popeye & Bluto's Bilge-Rat Barges, where water comes up through the raft floor.
Universal Studios Hollywood is built on a hillside with a long escalator run between the two levels. Pack for vertical distance, not just horizontal.

sections.heading: The locker problem, and what it changes
body: At Islands of Adventure, The Incredible Hulk Coaster, Jurassic World VelociCoaster, Hagrid's Magical Creatures Motorbike Adventure, Doctor Doom's Fearfall and Harry Potter and the Forbidden Journey all require you to store everything before boarding. At Universal Studios Florida, Revenge of the Mummy and Hollywood Rip Ride Rockit do the same. That is seven of the resort's most-ridden attractions, and it includes both parks' single most popular ride.

The policy is enforced properly. There are metal detectors at the platform on several of these, phones do come out of shorts pockets in inversions, and team members will send you back. Emptying every pocket is not optional and arguing about a zipped one wastes everybody's time.

The lockers are free for the posted duration, which is set to cover a normal ride cycle plus the queue you were already in. If the ride goes down while you are on it, that clock is generally handled — but the practical fix is to use the locker for as short a time as possible rather than to rely on grace.

The bank is the bottleneck. On a busy afternoon at Jurassic World VelociCoaster, the queue for the locker touchscreens can be longer than the queue to board. That is entirely avoidable and almost nobody avoids it: the answer is to arrive at the ride with nothing that has to go in one.

Water rides use a different arrangement — paid lockers with a longer duration, near the entrances, because you will be gone longer and you want somewhere dry to leave things. Budget for those separately and treat them as a service you are buying rather than an inconvenience.

items: Islands of Adventure, mandatory ride lockers: The Incredible Hulk Coaster, Jurassic World VelociCoaster, Hagrid's Magical Creatures Motorbike Adventure, Doctor Doom's Fearfall, Harry Potter and the Forbidden Journey.
Universal Studios Florida, mandatory ride lockers: Revenge of the Mummy, Hollywood Rip Ride Rockit.
Universal Studios Hollywood: lockers before Jurassic World — The Ride, plus a bank on the Upper Lot. Use them before you go down the Starway, not after.
Free for a posted duration, charged beyond it. The cost is not the problem; the queue for the touchscreens is.
Water rides use separate paid lockers near the entrances, with a longer duration. Treat those as a service worth paying for.
Empty every pocket before you reach the platform, including zipped ones. Metal detectors are in use and team members will send you back.

callout.title: The trick that beats the locker bank
callout.body: If anyone in your party is sitting out — using Child Swap, or waiting while the others ride single rider — they hold everything. Phones, bags, hats, sunglasses. Nobody in your group touches a locker all day. At The Incredible Hulk Coaster and Jurassic World VelociCoaster that alone saves twenty minutes, and it costs nothing but agreeing to it in advance.

sections.heading: The bag itself
body: Carry the smallest bag your day genuinely requires. A large backpack at Universal Orlando means a locker every time somebody wants to ride, which means the biggest queue of the day is one you joined voluntarily. A small crossbody or a compact sling is the right shape: it holds a phone, a card, sunscreen, a battery pack and a water bottle, and it fits in a small locker in one movement.

Wear shorts or trousers with fewer pockets rather than more. Every pocket is something you have to empty at seven rides, and cargo shorts are a genuine liability here in a way they are not anywhere else. Zip pockets are not an exemption.

Sunglasses and hats need a plan. Neither can go on any of the coasters. A cheap pair of sunglasses that you do not mind losing beats a good pair you will worry about, and a hat with no plan is a hat somebody will be holding for you all day.

Everything goes through bag check on entry at both resorts, so pack so that nothing needs unpacking. Glass containers are not permitted, and the rules on outside food and coolers are worth checking on the current prohibited items list rather than assuming — Universal publishes it and it is short.

items: A small crossbody or sling, not a backpack. It has to fit in a locker in one movement.
Shorts with fewer pockets. Every pocket is a delay at seven attractions.
Cheap sunglasses. Nothing you own can go on the coasters, and something will get lost.
A refillable water bottle. Universal Orlando in July is not a place to be buying every drink.
A card or phone payment rather than cash. Faster at the food windows and one less thing to lock away.
Check the current prohibited items list before you pack a cooler or anything glass.

sections.heading: Packing for the water rides
body: Universal's water rides are not decorative. Popeye & Bluto's Bilge-Rat Barges at Islands of Adventure will soak you through to the skin rather than mist you, and riders leave it wet to the underwear on a regular basis. Dudley Do-Right's Ripsaw Falls sends a wall of water over the front of the log on its final drop, which goes below the waterline. Jurassic Park River Adventure ends with an eighty-five-foot drop that drenches the front rows and dampens the back.

Ponchos help with Ripsaw Falls and do very little on the Barges, where water comes up through the floor of the raft rather than over the sides. Anyone selling you a poncho as the solution to Toon Lagoon has not ridden the Barges.

The tactic that works is to do both Toon Lagoon rides back to back in the early afternoon, with everything in a locker, in clothes you are happy to be wet in. In Florida in the afternoon that converts the worst two hours of the day into the best. Doing them at 10 AM converts the rest of the day into a slog in wet shoes.

Spare socks are the single most underrated thing in a Universal bag. They weigh nothing, they cost nothing, and dry socks change the entire back half of a day. A dry shirt for anyone under about twelve is the second.

At Universal Studios Hollywood the equivalent is Jurassic World — The Ride, with an eighty-four-foot drop and a front row that takes the worst of it. Use the lockers before you ride rather than after, and if you are doing the Lower Lot in the morning, do it before you are in dry clothes you care about.

items: Do Dudley Do-Right's Ripsaw Falls and Popeye & Bluto's Bilge-Rat Barges back to back, in the early afternoon.
Everything into a locker first. A phone in a shorts pocket on the Barges is a phone in the water.
Wear clothes that dry, not cotton that stays heavy for four hours.
Pack spare socks. This is the cheapest quality-of-life item in the bag.
A poncho for Ripsaw Falls. Do not expect it to do anything on the Barges.
A waterproof phone pouch if you have one — useful on Jurassic Park River Adventure where a locker is not always required.

callout.title: Soaked, not sprinkled
callout.body: Visitors who know the Disney water rides consistently underestimate these. Splash-level expectations set by a log flume do not apply to the Bilge-Rat Barges, which is the wettest ride in Orlando by a distance. Plan to change something, or plan to be wet for two hours.

sections.heading: Feet, terrain, and the Hollywood hill
body: Feet decide a park day more than any other packing decision, and the mistake is universal: new shoes, worn for the first time, on the day with the most walking in it. Bring shoes you have already walked ten miles in, and bring a second pair so you are not in the same ones two days running.

Universal Orlando's two original parks are flat and compact, which is genuinely easier than a Disney park — the walk between the Islands of Adventure and Universal Studios Florida entrances is about three minutes. Epic Universe is larger and the walk from the entrance out to the furthest world and back is real distance. None of it is difficult terrain.

Universal Studios Hollywood is the outlier and it catches people out. The park is built on a hillside and split across two levels connected by a long series of escalators known locally as the Starway. Each transit takes several minutes. Plan the day to minimise round trips rather than criss-crossing, and if anyone in your party tires on stairs or escalators, treat that as the constraint the day is built around.
Blister plasters in the bag, applied at the first hot spot rather than at the end of the day, is the difference between one bad afternoon and three.

items: Broken-in shoes, and a second pair for the second day.
Blister plasters, applied at the first hot spot rather than when it is already a blister.
Thin socks that dry, given the water rides.
At Universal Studios Hollywood, plan around the Starway. Do the Lower Lot in one block rather than going up and down.
At Epic Universe, budget for a longer walk from the entrance than the two original parks require.

sections.heading: Orlando humidity versus a Los Angeles hillside
body: These two resorts need different bags and it is worth packing for the one you are visiting rather than for a generic theme park.

Orlando from roughly May to October is hot and humid with near-daily afternoon thunderstorms. The rain arrives fast, lasts twenty to forty minutes, and stops as suddenly as it started. A poncho beats an umbrella, which you will spend the day carrying. The genuinely useful move is to plan the water rides for the same window as the storms and stop caring about either.

Sun exposure at Universal Orlando is worse than the shade cover suggests. The parks have less canopy than the Disney parks do, and Toon Lagoon, Marvel Super Hero Island and the Universal Studios Florida streets are open pavement. Sunscreen goes on before you leave the hotel and again at lunch, not once at 11 AM.

Los Angeles is dry heat, which is easier to walk in and much easier to underestimate. You dehydrate without feeling like you are sweating, evenings cool off sharply, and a layer for after dark is worth the space. Rain is rare outside winter and a poncho is usually dead weight.

callout.title: The bottle, not the cups
callout.body: A refillable bottle and the free ice water available at quick-service counters covers most of a day for nothing. Universal sells refillable cup programmes that are worth it for a large party on a long trip and are not worth it for two people on one day. Do that sum before you buy at the first cart you pass.

sections.heading: Packing with children
body: Strollers can be rented just inside the turnstiles at Islands of Adventure and at the other parks, and third-party rental companies deliver to Universal hotels for less across a multi-day trip. Park rentals sell out by mid-morning on busy days, which is worth knowing before you decide to rent on arrival.

The specifically Universal problem for families is that a stroller cannot come into the queue past a certain point and the child is walking the whole queue with you if you are using Child Swap. Pack accordingly: a drink and a plain snack that survives a warm bag, something quiet for a child to do, and a hat, because parts of these queues are outdoors.

One gallon-sized zip bag folded flat in the bottom of the bag, plus a spare shirt for anyone under ten. Universal's screen rides make more children unwell than Disney's do, and the day you need that bag you will need it immediately and in a queue. Keep both in a pocket rather than in the bag you will have to put in a locker.

Ear defenders are worth considering for noise-sensitive children. Universal's stunt shows are loud by design — explosions, gunfire and sustained volume — and several of the rides are engineered around volume spikes. A pair in the bag is cheaper than leaving a show early.

items: Rent a stroller from a third party delivered to your hotel rather than in-park, on any trip longer than a day.
One gallon zip bag and a spare shirt, kept out of the locker-bound bag.
A plain snack and a drink for the queue, since a child on Child Swap walks all of it with you.
Ear defenders for noise-sensitive children. The stunt shows are loud by design.
Sunscreen for children reapplied at lunch, not once in the morning.
Something small and quiet for a queue. Universal queues are good, and forty minutes is still forty minutes.

sections.heading: What to leave at home
body: The list of things not to bring matters more at Universal than at most parks, because the locker policy turns every unnecessary item into a repeated cost.

A large backpack is the headline. It buys you nothing you could not carry in a sling, and it costs you a locker interaction at seven attractions. The second is anything you would be upset to lose — good sunglasses, a hat you like, jewellery that could come off in an inversion.

Selfie sticks and similar extendable mounts are restricted, so leave them rather than discovering it at bag check. Glass containers are not permitted. The rules on outside food and coolers are published on Universal's own prohibited items list and are worth reading before you pack a lunch, because they change and because bag check is the wrong place to learn them.

Finally, leave the Disney planning apparatus at home too. There is no morning booking alarm to set, no dining scramble to prepare for, and nothing to refresh every thirty minutes. Universal asks for decisions before you arrive and very little while you are there, which is one of the genuinely nice things about it.

items: A large backpack. It costs you a locker queue at seven attractions and gains you nothing.
Good sunglasses, favourite hats and anything that could come off in an inversion.
Selfie sticks and extendable mounts, which are restricted.
Glass containers of any kind.
An umbrella in Orlando. A poncho does the job and leaves your hands free.
Cash as your primary payment. Card or phone is faster at every window and one less thing to lock away.

callout.title: One honest exception
callout.body: If your party includes someone who will not be riding the coasters — a grandparent, an adult with a bad back, a parent doing Child Swap all day — a larger bag becomes fine again, because it never has to go in a locker. Packing decisions at Universal are really decisions about who is riding what.

faqs.q: Why does Universal make you use lockers?
faqs.a: Because loose articles come out of pockets on rides with inversions and high forces, and at speed a phone is a projectile. Seven of the most-ridden attractions across the two original Orlando parks require everything to be stored before boarding, and the policy is enforced with metal detectors at the platform. Zipped pockets are not an exemption.

The mandatory ride lockers are free for a posted duration that covers your ride, and they charge beyond it. The water rides use separate paid lockers with a longer duration near the entrances. The cost is rarely the problem — the queue for the locker touchscreens on a busy afternoon can be longer than the queue to board.

faqs.q: What size bag should I bring to Universal?
faqs.a: The smallest one your day genuinely needs — a crossbody or a compact sling that fits into a locker in a single movement. A large backpack means a locker interaction at every coaster, which is the biggest avoidable queue of the day. If somebody in your party is sitting out the rides, they can carry more and nobody touches a locker at all.

faqs.q: How wet do the Universal water rides get you?
faqs.a: Genuinely soaked rather than sprinkled. Popeye & Bluto's Bilge-Rat Barges is the wettest ride in Orlando and riders regularly leave it wet to the skin. Dudley Do-Right's Ripsaw Falls sends a wall of water over the front of the log, and Jurassic Park River Adventure drenches the front rows on an eighty-five-foot drop. Bring spare socks.

On Dudley Do-Right's Ripsaw Falls, yes. On Popeye & Bluto's Bilge-Rat Barges, barely — the water comes up through the floor of the raft rather than over the sides. A poncho is genuinely useful for Florida afternoon thunderstorms from about June onward, which is a better reason to carry one.

faqs.q: Can I bring my own food and water into the park?
faqs.a: A refillable water bottle is straightforwardly worth carrying, and the free ice water at quick-service counters covers most of a day. The rules on outside food, coolers and glass containers are published on Universal's own prohibited items list, they change, and bag check is the wrong place to find out. Read it before you pack.

faqs.q: Is anything different for Universal Studios Hollywood?
faqs.a: Two things. The climate is dry heat with cool evenings, so a light layer for after dark is worth the space and a poncho usually is not. And the park is built on a hillside split across two levels joined by a long escalator run, so plan the day to minimise round trips and treat that as the constraint if anyone in your party tires on stairs.

faqs.q: What is the single most useful thing to pack?
faqs.a: Spare socks, and the smallest bag you can manage. The socks change the back half of a day after the water rides for almost no weight, and the small bag means you are never the party stuck at the locker touchscreens while everyone else walks onto the ride.
